latin: Sapientes Israhel post cessationem prophetiae per spiritum, prophetarunt per filiam uocis.
translation: The wise men of Israel, after the cessation of prophecy through the spirit, prophesied through the daughter of the voice.
translation_note: 'filiam uocis' is kept literal, 'daughter of the voice', calquing the rabbinic bat qol; Farmer glosses 'spirit'/'daughter of the voice' as higher and lower modes of prophecy flowing from the tenth sefirah, 'kingdom' (paraphrase, farmer1998:18429).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch12, from Latin at farmer1998:18402

sources.pico_relation: Wirszubski directs comparison of the thesis to this passage of Recanati

doctrine: Farmer's note, following the passage from Recanati cited by Wirszubski (1989: 51), glosses 'spirit' and 'daughter of the voice' as higher and lower modes of prophecy flowing from 'kingdom', the tenth and lowest sefirah, and states that the scheme fits a general view in Pico's historical theses of a systematic degradation of wisdom over time (paraphrase, farmer1998:18429).
historiography: Wirszubski quotes the thesis as his 'Conclusio XLV' under the heading 'Sources of the First Set of Theses' and directs comparison to Recanati, fol. 83va-b (wirszubski1989:2917, 2920).

quotations.text: Sapientes Israhel, post cessationem prophetiae per spiritum, prophetarunt per filiam uocis.

not_established: The content of Recanati, fol. 83va-b, beyond Wirszubski's cross-reference to it, is not established by the sources consulted.
The content of Wirszubski (1989: 51) on this thesis, cited by Farmer, is not otherwise in the excerpt consulted.
